revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Selling Pizzas
revealWordProblem.text:
At a local pizza shop, a customer can order a large pizza with up to three different toppings for $12.49. The shop is open daily from 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. and has a total of 6 employees. The shop spends $1.15 on cheese and $1.95 on sauce for each pizza.
Question: How would you describe the relationship between the number of large pizzas sold and each of the following: the hours the shop is open, the number of employees who work in the shop, the cost of cheese each week, and the cost of sauce each week?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A pizzeria sign showing hours of 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. and a large pizza with up to 3 toppings for $12.49.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Sort each pair by whether one quantity depends on the other. The hours the shop is open do not change when more pizzas sell — the shop is open 11 to 9 either way — so the hours are independent of pizza sales. The number of employees is also independent day to day; 6 people work whether the shop sells 40 pizzas or 90. Cheese cost does depend on pizzas sold: every pizza uses $1.15 of cheese, so weekly cheese cost = 1.15p, where p is the number of pizzas. Sauce works the same way at $1.95 a pizza, so weekly sauce cost = 1.95p. In both of those, p is the independent variable and the cost is the dependent variable, and each cost grows at a steady rate as p grows.

questions.stem: Akela chooses how many hours of sunlight each tray gets. Which is the INDEPENDENT variable?
questions.explanation: Akela chooses the sunlight, so sunlight is subject to choice — that makes it independent.
choiceFeedback: You have the two variables backward. Ask which one someone gets to CHOOSE — that one is independent.
The number of trays is not one of the two quantities being related here.
The number of seeds is not one of the two quantities being related here.
hints: Which quantity did Akela get to decide?
Sunlight was set by where she put the tray.
The one subject to choice is independent.
questions.stemEs: Akela escoge cuántas horas de luz solar recibe cada bandeja. ¿Cuál es la variable INDEPENDIENTE?
questions.explanationEs: Akela escoge la luz solar, así que la luz solar es lo que se escoge — eso la hace independiente.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál cantidad pudo decidir Akela?
La luz solar la determinó dónde puso la bandeja.
La que se escoge es la independiente.

questions.stem: In Akela's experiment, which is the DEPENDENT variable?
questions.explanation: Height responds to how much sunlight the tray received, so height is the dependent variable.
choiceFeedback: You have the two variables backward. Ask which one someone gets to CHOOSE — that one is independent.
The kind of seed was the same for all three trays.
The tray size was the same for all three trays.
hints: Which quantity RESPONDED to the other?
Akela did not choose how tall the plants grew.
The responding quantity is dependent.
questions.stemEs: En el experimento de Akela, ¿cuál es la variable DEPENDIENTE?

hintsEs: ¿Cuál cantidad RESPONDIÓ a la otra?
Akela no escogió qué tan alto crecieron las plantas.
La cantidad que responde es la dependiente.

level3.stem: Claire decides to walk instead of jog for the same 30 minutes. What happens to the two variables?
choices: Time stays the independent variable; Calories burned still depends on it
Calories burned becomes the independent variable
Neither is a variable any more
level3.explanation: Changing the activity changes how many Calories each minute burns, but time is still the quantity she chooses.
choiceFeedback: You have the two variables backward. Ask which one someone gets to CHOOSE — that one is independent.
Both quantities still change and are still related.
You have the two variables backward. Ask which one someone gets to CHOOSE — that one is independent.
hints: Does Claire still choose the minutes?
Yes — she sets the time either way.
The roles do not swap when the rate changes.

hintsEs: ¿Claire sigue escogiendo los minutos?

Los papeles no se intercambian cuando cambia la tasa.

level3.stem: If Claire runs exactly 3 miles and records how long it takes, which is the independent variable now?
level3.explanation: This time she fixes the distance by choice and the time is whatever results, so distance is independent and time is dependent.
choiceFeedback: Time is now the result, not the choice — the roles have flipped from the earlier problem.
Speed is not one of the two quantities she set or recorded.
Calories are not mentioned in this version of the problem.
hints: What did Claire decide in advance this time?
She decided the distance: 3 miles.
Whatever she measures afterward is the dependent one.
level3.stemEs: Si Claire corre exactamente 3 millas y registra cuánto tiempo tarda, ¿cuál es ahora la variable independiente?
level3.explanationEs: Esta vez ella fija la distancia por decisión y el tiempo es lo que resulte, así que la distancia es independiente y el tiempo es dependiente.
hintsEs: ¿Qué decidió Claire de antemano esta vez?
Ella decidió la distancia: 3 millas.
Lo que ella mida después es la dependiente.

level3.stem: A pizza shop decides each morning how many pizzas to make, then weighs out the cheese it needs. Devon says: “Cheese is the independent variable, because the shop buys the cheese before it makes any pizzas.” Devon is wrong. What rule did Devon use, and why does that rule fail here?
level3.stemEs: Una pizzería decide cada mañana cuántas pizzas va a hacer y luego pesa el queso que necesita. Devon dice: “El queso es la variable independiente, porque la pizzería compra el queso antes de hacer las pizzas”. Devon está equivocado. ¿Qué regla usó Devon y por qué esa regla falla aquí?
level3.modelAnswer: Devon used the rule “whatever happens first in time is the independent variable.” That rule fails because the roles depend on what is chosen, not on what happens first. The shop chooses the number of pizzas, so pizzas is the independent variable, and the cheese used responds to that choice — cheese is dependent.
level3.modelAnswerEs: Devon usó la regla “lo que ocurre primero en el tiempo es la variable independiente”. Esa regla falla porque los papeles dependen de lo que se elige, no de lo que ocurre primero. La pizzería elige el número de pizzas, así que las pizzas son la variable independiente, y el queso usado responde a esa elección — el queso es dependiente.

level3.stem: Claim: “The dependent variable always has the larger values.” Is this claim always, sometimes, or never true?
level3.stemEs: Afirmación: “La variable dependiente siempre tiene los valores más grandes”. ¿Esta afirmación es siempre, a veces o nunca verdadera?
choices: Sometimes — the size of the numbers has nothing to do with which variable is which
Always — the dependent variable is the result, so it is bigger
Never — the independent variable is always the larger one
Only when both quantities are measured in the same unit
choicesEs: A veces — el tamaño de los números no tiene nada que ver con cuál variable es cuál
Siempre — la variable dependiente es el resultado, así que es más grande
Nunca — la variable independiente siempre es la más grande
Solo cuando ambas cantidades se miden en la misma unidad
level3.explanation: Sometimes. Jog for 90 minutes and you might run 9 miles — the dependent value (9) is smaller. Give a plant 3 hours of sunlight and it might reach 12 cm — the dependent value (12) is larger. The role is decided by which quantity is subject to choice, not by which numbers are bigger.
level3.explanationEs: A veces. Si trotas 90 minutos podrías correr 9 millas — el valor dependiente (9) es más pequeño. Si le das a una planta 3 horas de sol podría llegar a 12 cm — el valor dependiente (12) es más grande. El papel lo decide cuál cantidad se elige, no cuáles números son más grandes.
choiceFeedback: Find one case where the dependent value is smaller — 90 minutes of jogging, 9 miles run — and the claim breaks.
That is the same mistake in reverse. Try to find a case where the dependent value is larger.
Units do not decide the roles either. 90 minutes → 9 miles uses different units and the dependent value is still smaller.
hints: Try to find ONE example where the claim is false. One is enough to rule out “always”.
Jog 90 minutes and run 9 miles. Which value is larger — the one you chose, or the one that responded?
hintsEs: Intenta encontrar UN ejemplo donde la afirmación sea falsa. Uno basta para descartar “siempre”.
Trota 90 minutos y corre 9 millas. ¿Cuál valor es más grande — el que elegiste o el que respondió?

level3.stem: Describe one situation where time is the independent variable, and a different situation where time is the dependent variable. For each one, say who or what does the choosing.
level3.stemEs: Describe una situación donde el tiempo sea la variable independiente y una situación distinta donde el tiempo sea la variable dependiente. En cada una, di quién o qué hace la elección.
level3.modelAnswer: Independent: I choose to jog for 30 minutes and see how many Calories I burn. I chose the time, so time is independent and Calories depend on it. Dependent: I run exactly 3 miles and record how long it takes. I chose the distance, so time responded — time is dependent. Same quantity, opposite roles, because a different thing was chosen each time.
level3.modelAnswerEs: Independiente: elijo trotar 30 minutos y veo cuántas calorías quemo. Yo elegí el tiempo, así que el tiempo es independiente y las calorías dependen de él. Dependiente: corro exactamente 3 millas y registro cuánto tardo. Yo elegí la distancia, así que el tiempo respondió — el tiempo es dependiente. La misma cantidad, papeles opuestos, porque en cada caso se eligió algo distinto.

level3.stem: Here is the result of an experiment: “Water temperature depends on how long the pot has been on the stove.” Working backwards, describe the experiment. What would you choose, what would you measure, and what would the two column headings of your table be?
level3.stemEs: Este es el resultado de un experimento: “La temperatura del agua depende de cuánto tiempo lleva la olla en la estufa”. Trabajando al revés, describe el experimento. ¿Qué elegirías, qué medirías y cuáles serían los dos encabezados de las columnas de tu tabla?
level3.modelAnswer: I would choose the number of minutes the pot stays on the stove — that is the independent variable, because I decide it. I would measure the water temperature at each of those times — that is the dependent variable, because it responds. My table's columns would be “Minutes on the stove” and “Water temperature (°C)”, with the chosen quantity in the first column.
level3.modelAnswerEs: Elegiría el número de minutos que la olla permanece en la estufa — esa es la variable independiente, porque yo la decido. Mediría la temperatura del agua en cada uno de esos momentos — esa es la variable dependiente, porque responde. Las columnas de mi tabla serían “Minutos en la estufa” y “Temperatura del agua (°C)”, con la cantidad elegida en la primera columna.
